_comment: Hand-verified compat implementations, same standard as members.overrides.json: each entry exists because the old member is GONE from 26.2, a faithful reimplementation was found by reading the 26.2 jar with javap, and the evidence is written down so it can be argued with. jar-bridge compiles these against the real target jars, so a recipe that stops being true stops compiling rather than silently shipping.

recipes.name: getColor
recipes.body: net.minecraft.network.chat.TextColor c = net.minecraft.network.chat.TextColor.fromLegacyFormat(self); return c == null ? null : java.lang.Integer.valueOf(c.getValue());
recipes.evidence: 26.2 removed ChatFormatting.getColor(). TextColor.fromLegacyFormat(ChatFormatting) exists in 26.2 and returns null for non-colour formats, which matches getColor()'s old contract of null for BOLD/ITALIC/etc; getValue() is the int. Verified by javap against the 26.2 jar.

recipes.name: exists
recipes.evidence: 26.2 reduced I18n to get() only. I18n.exists always delegated to the language map; Language.getInstance().has(String) is declared in the 26.2 jar and answers the same question. Verified by javap.

classes.name: foxgrade/Tuple
classes.evidence: 26.2 deleted net.minecraft.util.Tuple outright — no same-name class anywhere in the jar, no unique same-member replacement. Its whole API is five trivial members (javap of the 26.1 jar), so the honest fix is to ship the class: it is our build of the mod, and a pair type carries no game behaviour.
source: private A a; private B b;
public Tuple(A a, B b) { this.a = a; this.b = b; }
public void setA(A a) { this.a = a; }
public void setB(B b) { this.b = b; }
